Subject: Re: Performance SLO follow-up: p95/p99 end-to-end latency (hosted API vs current provider)

Hi Sam — great conversation this morning, thanks for the time. Quick recap and a couple follow-ups so we can scope a short performance validation: 

1) Recap from the call
- Primary goal: validate end-to-end latency under real workload (user-facing p95/p99) and confirm streaming chunk latency for the portions of your product that rely on low-latency token streaming.
- Current pain: variability at p99 causing occasional UI stalls; want predictable tails under production concurrency.

2) Clarifying questions (attached spreadsheet with details):
- Typical request size: prompt ~ 120 tokens, expected completion ~ 60 tokens (total ~ 180 tokens).
- Target throughput/concurrency: baseline production 120 req/s with steady concurrency ~60; expected spike up to 250 req/s during peak. Can you confirm average request/response token counts?
- Streaming usage: you mentioned ~30% of calls use streaming (real-time transcript). For streaming calls we need per-chunk latency target (e.g., chunk RTT < 100ms).
- SLO targets you want to validate against: is p95 <= 200ms and p99 <= 500ms a fair starting point, or are you aiming tighter?

3) Proposed next steps
- You send current provider p95/p99 baseline (end-to-end) and any perf reports — we can use that to calibrate the test.
- We run a 48–72 hour validation on our hosted API with a mirrored workload (smoke -> stress -> streaming validation).
- Quick sync to align the exact test payloads and networking (we may want to run from your region/egress).

Attachments: 20260615-slo-questions.xlsx (questions matrix), redwood-hosted-baseline.pdf (example hosted baseline numbers & methodology).

If the above looks right I can get Aditya (infra perf) looped in to draft the test plan and schedule. Available for a 30-min sync today or tomorrow afternoon.

Thanks,
Marissa

Subject: Re: Performance SLO follow-up: p95/p99 end-to-end latency (hosted API vs current provider)

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. Answers inline below and attaching our most recent provider report.

- Typical token sizes: prompt ~ 100–130 tokens, completion ~50–80 tokens (so your 180-token estimate is about right).
- Current provider baseline (end-to-end, measured at our edge): synchronous API calls (non-streaming) at avg load ~120 req/s, concurrency ~60: p50=110ms, p95=420ms, p99=930ms.
- Throughput & spikes: steady 120 req/s, bursts up to ~260 req/s for short windows (1–3 minutes).
- Streaming: ~30% of calls use streaming. For streaming, typical chunk size is 32 tokens; observed chunk RTTs between 80–140ms depending on region and network. The user-visible experience degrades when chunk RTT exceeds ~200ms.
- Network/topology: we run regional front doors in us-west and us-east; egress to providers is via our cloud egress (I attached a simple diagram).

Attachments: finlytics-current-slo-report.pdf, network-topology.png

Goal: Ideally we want hosted p95 <= 200ms and p99 <= 500ms for the common sync calls; for streaming, chunk RTT <= 120ms at p95. If Redwood can show comparable or better numbers under a mirrored workload, we can move toward a short contract to run a pilot.

Happy to hop on a call to pick test windows. Wed/Thu this week are best for me.

—Sam

Subject: Re: Performance SLO follow-up: p95/p99 end-to-end latency (hosted API vs current provider)

Thanks — this is exactly what we needed. Quick follow-up on our side and a proposed plan: 

1) Redwood hosted baseline (what we typically see for comparable model & token sizes):
- Synchronous (non-streaming): p50 ~ 80–120ms, p95 ~ 160–220ms, p99 ~ 320–480ms (range depends on model variant, sequence length, and whether KV cache hits occur).
- Streaming: per-chunk RTT p50 ~ 40–70ms, p95 ~ 80–120ms; end-to-end perceived latency depends on chunk cadence and network (we typically aim for chunk RTT p95 <= 120ms).

2) Proposed validation plan (attached): proposed-perf-test-plan.pdf
- Phase A (smoke): 1k calls across 10 minutes to confirm payloads and headers, validate correctness and instrumentation.
- Phase B (baseline): steady load 120 req/s, concurrency 60 for 3 hours to capture steady-state p95/p99 and resource utilization.
- Phase C (stress): short bursts to 250–300 req/s for 10–15 minutes to observe tail behavior and autoscaling/fallback response.
- Phase D (streaming): run streaming subset at production ratio (~30%) validating chunk RTT distribution and UX threshold.

3) Instrumentation & pass/fail
- We will provide a results dashboard and raw sample logs (redacted) showing end-to-end timing from client -> edge -> model -> response. Pass criteria: end-to-end p95 <= 200ms and p99 <= 500ms for sync calls; streaming chunk RTT p95 <= 120ms.

4) Logistics
- We can run the test from our us-west region and also from a mirror in us-east if you want region comparisons.
- Suggested window: 48 hours starting once we finalize payloads and network egress settings.

Next steps: if you can confirm the token sizes (you already did — thanks) and give a final go for Wed 16 Jun start, Aditya will provision the test harness and send the detailed runner config. I dropped a draft mutual action plan here: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aB2cPerfPlanExample (will update with exact run times).

Attachments: proposed-perf-test-plan.pdf

Would Wed 16 Jun at 10:00 PT for a 30-min kickoff work for you?

Thanks,
Marissa
